interpretations: Count distinct orders with at least one invoice for each gender represented among those orders, treating NULL gender as a group; average those counts, then return the mean count and mean excess for genders strictly above that average.

Count distinct orders with at least one invoice for every gender represented in Customers, including genders with zero invoiced orders and NULL gender; average those counts, then return the mean count and mean excess for genders strictly above that average.

Count invoices for each gender represented among invoiced orders, so an order with multiple invoices contributes multiple times; average those counts, then return the mean count and mean excess for genders strictly above that average.

Count invoices for every gender represented in Customers, including genders with zero invoices; average those counts, then return the mean count and mean excess for genders strictly above that average.

Count distinct invoiced orders by gender, treating both NULL and an empty gender value as one missing-gender group; use only groups with invoiced orders when calculating the average and the two requested results.

queries:
WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(order_count) AS mean_count
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT
    AVG(gc.order_count) AS mean_count,
    AVG(gc.order_count - om.mean_count) AS mean_excess
FROM gender_counts AS gc
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS om
WHERE gc.order_count > om.mean_count

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender,
           COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN i.invoice_number IS NOT NULL THEN o.order_id END) AS invoiced_orders
    FROM Customers AS c
    LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
gender_average AS (
    SELECT AVG(invoiced_orders) AS average_count
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT AVG(gc.invoiced_orders) AS mean_count,
       AVG(gc.invoiced_orders - ga.average_count) AS mean_excess
FROM gender_counts AS gc
CROSS JOIN gender_average AS ga
WHERE gc.invoiced_orders > ga.average_count

WITH gender_counts AS (
    SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count
    FROM Invoices AS i
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.gender
),
overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(invoice_count) AS mean_count
    FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT AVG(gc.invoice_count) AS mean_count,
       AVG(gc.invoice_count - om.mean_count) AS mean_excess
FROM gender_counts AS gc
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS om
WHERE gc.invoice_count > om.mean_count

WITH gender_counts AS (
  SELECT c.gender, COUNT(i.invoice_number) AS invoice_count
  FROM Customers AS c
  LEFT JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  LEFT JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  GROUP BY c.gender
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(invoice_count) AS invoice_count FROM gender_counts
)
SELECT
  AVG(g.invoice_count) AS mean_count,
  AVG(g.invoice_count - m.invoice_count) AS mean_excess
FROM gender_counts AS g
CROSS JOIN overall_mean AS m
WHERE g.invoice_count > m.invoice_count

WITH invoiced_orders_by_gender AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(NULLIF(c.gender, ''), 'Missing') AS gender,
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS invoiced_order_count
    FROM Customers AS c
    JOIN Orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN Invoices AS i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
    GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(c.gender, ''), 'Missing')
)
SELECT
    gender,
    invoiced_order_count,
    AVG(invoiced_order_count) OVER () AS average_invoiced_order_count
FROM invoiced_orders_by_gender
